results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * ol.quantity))::numeric, 2) AS total_gross_profit, ROUND(SUM((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1)::numeric, 2) AS total_ex_gst_revenue, ROUND((SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * ol.quantity)) / NULLIF(SUM((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_percentage FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32%, based on a total gross profit of $1,584,502.69 from $2,716,823.41 in ex-GST revenue. This calculation includes all non-voided orders, though product variants with missing cost data were excluded from the analysis.
results.assumptions: Calculated overall gross profit margin across all non-voided orders by taking ex-GST revenue minus total unit costs (ex-GST), divided by ex-GST revenue. Variants with NULL cost were excluded.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, round(sum(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * ol.quantity))::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5;
results.answer: Your top 5 products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit ($165,884.48), Shirt Dress ($130,441.22), Straw Hat ($108,854.01), High-Rise Jeans ($104,531.12), and Wool Coat ($89,912.11). This ranking excludes voided orders and products missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross profit as (line revenue ex-GST) minus (unit cost ex-GST * quantity). Excluded variants with NULL cost and orders with financial_status = 'voided'. Revenue is based on historical unit_price and line_discount.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(o.total_revenue, 0) - COALESCE(r.total_refunds, 2), 2) AS net_revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(o.total_revenue, 0), 2) AS gross_revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(r.total_refunds, 0), 2) AS total_refunds FROM (SELECT SUM(total) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided') o CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_refunds FROM refunds) r
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds for the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, was $3,205,298.79 AUD. This is based on a total gross revenue of $3,321,930.71 AUD minus $116,631.92 AUD in total refunds. This calculation includes all non-voided orders across the entire data period provided.
results.assumptions: Calculated net revenue for the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) by taking total gross revenue from non-voided orders and subtracting total refund amounts.

results.answer: Out of 17,340 valid orders, 5.7% (or 988 orders) had at least one refund. This calculation excludes voided orders from the total count.

results.question: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, SUM(rl.quantity) AS units_refunded FROM refund_lines rl JOIN order_lines ol ON rl.order_line_id = ol.order_line_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_refunded DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The One-Piece Swimsuit had the most units refunded, with a total of 165 units across all time periods in the dataset. This count is based on summed data from all available refund lines.
results.assumptions: Units refunded are summed from refund_lines across all time periods in the dataset.

results.question: How many different customers have placed an order?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers_with_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: You have had 2,909 different customers place an order. This count is based on unique customer IDs from non-voided orders. Please note that this total excludes guest checkouts, which make up about 22% of your orders, and some customers may be counted more than once if they used different details.
results.assumptions: Counted unique customer IDs from non-voided orders. ~22% of orders are guest checkouts (NULL customer_id) and some customers may share names/emails across multiple customer_id records, which is noted as a caveat in the schema.

results.question: What percentage of orders were placed by guests with no customer account?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS guest_order_percentage, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS guest_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Guests placed 22.47% of your orders, translating to 3,896 out of your 17,340 total non-voided orders. This calculation includes all available data across the entire dataset without any date filters applied.
results.assumptions: Calculated the percentage of orders placed by guests (where customer_id is NULL) out of all non-voided orders across the entire dataset.

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(total)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= timestamp '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < timestamp '2026-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') ORDER BY month ASC;
results.answer: Your revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 AUD in July, $282,129.97 AUD in August, and $278,068.87 AUD in September 2026. These figures include all non-voided orders grouped by month in Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Treating today as 2026-09-30, the last 3 months are July, August, and September 2026. Revenue is calculated as the sum of total for non-voided orders, grouped by month in Sydney time.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
    SUM(total) AS total_revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-06 00:00:00'
),
pre_eofy AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (2 Jun - 18 Jun)' AS period,
    SUM(total) AS total_revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-02 00:00:00'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
)
SELECT * FROM eofy_sales
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM pre_eofy;
results.answer: Revenue during the EOFY sale was significantly higher at $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders, compared to $186,171.83 from 794 orders in the 17 days right before it. This comparison assumes revenue is based on gross order totals for non-voided orders over two equal 17-day periods.
results.assumptions: Compared the 17-day EOFY sale period (2026-06-19 to 2025-07-05 inclusive of end date boundary) with the immediately preceding 17 days (2026-06-02 to 2026-06-18). Revenue is defined as gross order total for non-voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines ol ON v.variant_id = ol.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC LIMIT 3;
results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These totals cover all sales channels and exclude voided orders across the entire available data period.
results.assumptions: Calculated total units sold across all channels for non-voided orders over the entire available data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3) t
results.answer: A total of 1,640 registered customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders. This count excludes guest checkouts because they are not linked to a customer profile.
results.assumptions: Counted unique registered customers (customer_id IS NOT NULL) who have placed 3 or more non-voided orders. Guest checkouts (customer_id IS NULL) are excluded because they are not linked to a customer profile.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation looks at the time difference between when every order and its corresponding refund were created.
results.assumptions: Calculated the difference in days between the order creation timestamp and the refund creation timestamp for all refund events, and averaged them.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS discounted_revenue, COUNT(order_id) AS discounted_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND discount_id IS NOT NULL
results.answer: You made $944,363.46 in revenue from 5,279 orders that used a discount. This total covers all non-voided orders with a discount applied from October 2025 to September 2026.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the total of non-voided orders that had any discount applied (where discount_id is not null). Data covers the entire recorded period from October 2025 to September 2026.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: During the winter months of June to August 2026, the colour that sold the most units was Camel, with a total of 1,050 units sold. This excludes any voided orders based on Sydney local time.
results.assumptions: Winter is defined as June, July, and August 2026 based on Australian seasons, converted to Sydney local time. Voided orders are excluded.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, ROUND(SUM(o.total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY day_type ORDER BY day_type;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more total revenue than weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 from 6,187 orders on weekends. This comparison includes all non-voided orders based on local Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Compared total revenue and order counts for weekends (Saturday and Sunday) versus weekdays (Monday to Friday) for all non-voided orders, using Australia/Sydney local time.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(ol.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines ol ON v.variant_id = ol.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title, total_units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY product_type;
results.answer: The best-selling product overall is the One-Piece Swimsuit in swimwear with 4,043 units sold, while the top sellers for other categories range from 526 units for the Merino Crew Jumper in knitwear to 3,619 units for the Straw Hat in accessories. These totals count all units from non-voided orders grouped by lowercase product type.
results.assumptions: Best-selling is measured by total units sold across all non-voided orders, grouped by the lowercased product type.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_with_multiple_units FROM (SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING SUM(ol.quantity) > 1) AS multi_unit_orders
results.answer: There were 8,908 orders that contained more than one unit in total. This count includes only non-voided orders where the combined quantity of all items in the order was strictly greater than one.
results.assumptions: Counted orders where the sum of quantities across all order lines for a single non-voided order is strictly greater than 1.

results.question: How have sales of the cotton blue dress shirt changed over the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date AS month, sum(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) AS revenue, sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND p.product_type = 'top' AND (p.title ILIKE '%shirt%' OR p.title ILIKE '%blouse%') AND (v.color ILIKE '%navy%' OR v.color ILIKE '%cobalt%' OR v.color ILIKE '%blue%') AND o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AND o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
results.answer: Sales for your blue shirts (using our closest matching items like linen and poplin shirts) grew over the last two months, going from $114.95 (1 unit) in August to $408.07 (4 units) in September. There were no recorded sales for July. Please note that since you don't carry an exact "cotton blue dress shirt," these figures are based on items with "shirt" or "blouse" in the title and blue-family colors.
results.assumptions: The store has no 'cotton blue dress shirt' exactly, so we mapped it to tops with 'shirt' or 'blouse' in the title and blue-family colors (Navy, Cobalt) such as the 'Linen Shirt' or 'Oversized Poplin Shirt'. Last 3 months covers July, August, and September 2026 (data ends 2026-09-30). Revenue is gross order line revenue excluding voided orders.
